subject: Startups
title: What Is Growth Hacking?
description: A 60-second lesson on What Is Growth Hacking?.

hook.text: Sean Ellis coined 'growth hacker' in 2010. He needed a term for marketers obsessed with scalable, testable growth.

buildup.text: Traditional marketing buys ads. Growth hacking finds clever, cheap ways to grow by baking growth into the product.

discovery.text: Dropbox didn't buy ads. It offered free storage for referrals. The product itself became the marketing engine.

twist.text: Growth hacking isn't just tricks. It's a mindset: treat growth as an experiment, measure everything, iterate fast.

climax.text: The biggest startups all had growth hacks. Hotmail, Airbnb, and Slack each found one key lever and pulled hard.

punchline.text: Growth hacking turns the product into its own ad.
